form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.

form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

existence.reason: While CSE701 covers aspects of AI in Software Engineering such as automated testing and code review assistance, the new course focuses specifically on modern AI-native software development, agentic workflows, model context protocols (MCP), and human-agent collaborative loops rather than general mining of software repositories or general AI applications in SE.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course, serving as an applied, workflow-oriented follow-up to software engineering principles.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 examines data-driven software engineering and research literature on AI in SE, whereas the new course centers on hands-on, agentic development workflows, MCP, and practical tool use.

CSE594A emphasizes agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem solving, whereas the new course focuses specifically on software development processes, engineering practices, and developer workflows.
CSE582 deals with software product lines, maintenance, and traditional software re-engineering, whereas the new course addresses AI-native methods and autonomous coding tools.
CSE581 focuses on systems analysis and traditional requirements engineering theory, whereas the new course focuses on spec-driven development using AI coding agents.
AI501 is a core machine learning theory course, whereas the new course applies engineering practices and tools without teaching foundational machine learning models.
CSE201 provides foundational object-oriented programming and traditional unit testing, which the new course builds upon by introducing AI-assisted and automated testing workflows.

prerequisites.justification: Students require strong software development fundamentals, object-oriented concepts, and basic testing skills to effectively build and evaluate AI-assisted software projects.

resource_policy.reason: Because AI-native software development and coding agents are rapidly evolving domains, the course utilizes a mix of established reference textbooks on design patterns and software engineering, alongside recent peer-reviewed conference proceedings and research papers covering agentic design patterns and automated program repair.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. This course is designed for third and fourth-year undergraduate students in the Computer Science and Engineering programme who possess strong programming and software development fundamentals. Upon completing the course, students will be able to configure agent infrastructure and tools, deconstruct feature requests into executable specifications, implement iterative development loops and software factories, assess the reliability and correctness of agent-generated code, and design AI-native software development processes for multi-module application problems. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions, supported by hands-on projects and assignments.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules follow a logical progression from foundational tooling to advanced process design, building upon the mandatory prerequisite course CSE201 which provides software development and unit testing fundamentals.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprising quizzes, assignments, mid-semester exams, reports, and a capstone project aligns with the practical, workflow-oriented learning outcomes and emphasis on hands-on coding and evaluation.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which focuses on data-driven software engineering literature, CSE594A which emphasizes algorithmic reasoning, or traditional software engineering courses like CSE582 and CSE581, this course specifically centres on hands-on agentic development workflows, Model Context Protocol, and practical AI-native engineering practices.
